title: Whats the best workflow for animations for UE5?
author: vemelon
selftext: As the title says I need custom animations to import in Unreal Engine 5. Im working mainly with Claude Code and its not good to create animations directly in Unreal Engine. I need a better solution. For example I need a realistic animation for a human that gets shot in the neck and then he grabs his neck and slowly trips and falls to death. Any help?

comments.author: Crunchfest3
comments.body: Is this a scripted scene or something that needs to work anywhere during gameplay? For a scripted scene, I'd block out the reach, stagger, and fall as one performance first. Getting the hand contact and weight shift right matters more here than generating lots of motion. Gameplay would also need transitions from different starting poses.

replies.author: vemelon
replies.body: It needs to work everywhere as a death animation.

replies.author: Crunchfest3
replies.body: For that neck-grab, I'd keep the reach and stagger authored, then test a blend into ragdoll for the collapse. That gives you control over the gesture without forcing every body to land in the same pose, especially near walls or stairs. UE supports [blending animation with physics](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/physics-driven-animation-in-unreal-engine?lang=en-US). You'd still need a good source clip for the acting itself.

replies.author: vemelon
replies.body:
Thanks, that matches what I had in mind: authored reach and stagger, then Physics Control taking over for the collapse.

My real question is the step before that. I’ll record the acting myself with a single camera, no suit. What’s a good way to get from that video to a clean animation on the UE5 Mannequin?

Things I’m unsure about:

* Which video-to-mocap tool gives usable results for this kind of motion? I’ve seen Rokoko Vision, [Move.ai](http://Move.ai), DeepMotion and Tripo. Some open source ones (GVHMR, SMPL-X based) are non-commercial only, and this is going on Steam.
* How much cleanup should I expect? I’m thinking foot sliding, jitter, and especially the hands actually staying on the neck.
* Where do you do the cleanup? Blender, or directly in UE with Control Rig or IK Retargeter?
* Any tips for the recording itself? Camera distance, frame rate, clothing, one long take or short separate clips?

replies.author: Crunchfest3
replies.body: Ah, got it. I'd test a short reach-and-hold clip in Rokoko Vision and DeepMotion before recording the full death sequence. Compare them after retargeting onto your actual mannequin: does the wrist stay at the throat while the torso bends? DeepMotion's own [hand-tracking notes](https://www.deepmotion.com/post/animate-3d-hand-tracking-faq) flag hands touching the body as a weak spot, so I'd budget for manual contact cleanup. I'd use IK Retargeter for the transfer, then [Control Rig in Sequencer](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/animating-with-control-rig-in-unreal-engine?lang=en-US) to adjust the hand contact on the final proportions. For recording, use a fixed camera, keep the whole body visible and avoid loose clothes hiding the joints. The short test should tell you more about cleanup time than a provider's smoothest demo.
